clue.text: One beating an ace? Say why this is worthless

parts.note: in cards, a player who plays a trump can beat even an ace

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the following word and keep only its sound

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced exactly like the word why

explanation.surface: A card player muses that whoever beats an ace has made it worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game sets the scene, so the solver hunts for an adjective about cards; the definition is the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery is showy rubbish, things of no value, so as an adjective it means worthless.

clue.text: Emperor's sovereignty in India Brown's written about

definitions.note: the 's is a link, the definition is the emperor

indicators.note: something written about another thing is wrapped around it, so the colour encloses the rule

parts.note: tan is a light brown
the Raj was British sovereignty over India

explanation.surface: A historian named Brown has written on the empire's rule over India.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like a writer's surname; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor of the second century, famous for his column in Rome.

clue.text: Song I cut right out at first — rash!

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
at first places the rearranged letters before the song

parts.note: I, cut and R for right, rearranged
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A singer recklessly drops a number from the start of the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Rash looks like an adjective for the hasty cut; it is a noun, a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the medical name for hives, a raised itchy skin eruption.

clue.text: Something manufactured for the channel

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: Goods are being made for shipping across the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The channel suggests the sea between England and France; it is a mere pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is any item made by a factory or industrial process.

clue.text: Perch in the tidal race

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place where birds settle to sleep
second meaning: a strong tidal current, a word used in Orkney and Shetland

explanation.walkthrough: Perch could be a fish swimming in the race; instead it is a bird's resting place. Sumburgh Roost off Shetland is a famous tidal race.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a birds' sleeping place and a turbulent tidal current in northern Scottish waters.

clue.text: Out-of-the-way sort of role for a stableman

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so these letters come in a different order
out of here means placed outside, so the rearranged word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: role with its letters rearranged
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A remote, rather odd job is offered to someone who works with horses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was the groom at an inn who looked after travellers' horses, so a stableman.

clue.text: Initially some horrible liver disorder makes us become wizened

indicators.note: disorder means confusion, so the organ's letters are jumbled
initially points to the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
the organ rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty liver complaint is said to leave its sufferers shrunken and lined.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to shrink and wrinkle as moisture is lost, which is to grow wizened.

clue.text: Sort of early bird (female of the species)

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant form of it, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters of early, rearranged

explanation.surface: A hen is a kind of early riser, the female of her species.
explanation.walkthrough: Early bird reads as a person up at dawn; early is the raw material, and the bird with its bracket is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry keepers call a hen kept for eggs by this name, since she produces them daily.

clue.text: Freed from anxiety, as was, in a word, Lady Smith

definitions.text: as was, in a word, Lady Smith
definitions.meaning: second meaning: written as one word, Ladysmith is the South African town besieged in the Boer War and freed by British forces in 1900

explanation.walkthrough: Lady Smith looks like a person; in a word tells you to join it into Ladysmith, the besieged town whose rescue was cheered across Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means eased of worry, and also rescued from a siege, as the town of Ladysmith was.

clue.text: A recent Russian leader turns out to be an apostate

indicators.note: turns out suggests something turned over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the nationality is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A newly installed Kremlin chief proves to have abandoned the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader here is the first letter, not a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A recreant is someone who abandons a faith or cause, a deserter of their beliefs.

clue.text: Early star or moon deviations interest him

definitions.text: Early star or moon deviations interest him

indicators.note: deviations are departures from a set course, so the letters wander from their printed order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these four words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone is fascinated by a dawn star and irregularities in the moon's orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the letters to rearrange and a description of the person: the Astronomer Royal is the senior astronomer to the British monarch, whose post began at Greenwich Observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying the orbits of the moon and the motions of stars was the founding task of Britain's royal observatory post.

clue.text: Bill's story

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a statement of money owed
second meaning: a narrative or report of events

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a man called Bill telling his tale; the two nouns are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an invoice listing charges and a spoken or written report of what happened.

clue.text: Language used by clergyman? Just the opposite

parts.note: Rev is the short form of Reverend, a clergyman's title
Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone asks what tongue a vicar speaks, then answers that it is the contrary.
explanation.walkthrough: The language comes first in the clue but second in the answer, because it is used by, so placed after, the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of something is its contrary, exactly the other way round from it.

clue.text: Standards given by writer out west in US Intelligence

indicators.note: in places what precedes it inside the intelligence agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the United States

indicators.note: out means removed, so the compass point named next is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Guidelines are issued by an author who has left the west to join American intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the principles or benchmarks by which things are judged, the plural of criterion.

clue.text: Memento of what's left after a removal

indicators.note: after a removal tells you the single letter a is taken out of the word just named

parts.note: the remainder is whatever is left over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keepsake from what remained after moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: Removal looks like a house move; it signals that the letter a is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir that brings a person or event back to mind, a prompt to memory.

clue.text: Pupils in 12 describing money taken before recess

definitions.note: pupils read in reverse (12-across) is slip-up, a noun like the answer

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, the sum of money
an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: Students in a church are said to be watching cash go in the collection before the alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 12-across is REVERSE, so the definition is the word pupils spelt backwards: SLIPUP. Only then does the answer emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a small error or momentary failure, which is a slip-up.

clue.text: Like a society formed to supply the National Trust

parts.note: to supply is to provide
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A club is set up to furnish Britain's heritage charity.
explanation.walkthrough: A provident society is a British mutual body whose members save together against sickness or old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident societies are mutual savings bodies, named for the quality of saving for the future.

clue.text: Grotesque figure of Gog (7 version)

indicators.note: a version is another form of something, so the letters appear in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 7-down

explanation.surface: A monstrous effigy of Gog, the legendary giant, made in another form.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall, so a grotesque figure of Gog sounds like one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque face or creature on a building, often a waterspout.

clue.text: Danger signal makes all but fifty prepare for battle

indicators.note: all but means everything except, so the item named after it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
L is fifty in Roman numerals
to arm is to equip with weapons ready to fight

explanation.surface: A warning sends nearly everyone, bar fifty soldiers, to get ready to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a bell, siren or call that warns people of approaching peril.

clue.text: Islander is sort of cross

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a native of a Mediterranean island south of Sicily
second meaning: the eight-pointed cross of the Knights of St John

explanation.surface: Someone from an island is in a bit of a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like the adjective angry; it is the emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Malta is Maltese, and the Maltese cross is a famous emblem with four arrowhead arms.

clue.text: The case for a striker — or an arsonist?

definitions.text: The case for a striker — or an arsonist?

parts.note: surface reading: a legal argument made on behalf of a worker on strike
setter's reading: the striker is something struck to make a flame, so its case is the small container an arsonist might carry

explanation.surface: A lawyer weighs up defending a picketing worker, or perhaps a fire-raiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Case and striker both look like courtroom and industrial words; a striker is a match, and the case holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches come packed in a small cardboard container, and anyone starting a fire would need one.

clue.text: The rain worried the lock-keeper

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and churned about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: all seven letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A wet spell troubled the person who tends a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: A lock-keeper suggests a canal worker; here locks are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the head holds tresses of hair in place, so it keeps the locks.

clue.text: Diana gets many upset, being so unemotional

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana
lots means many

explanation.surface: Diana is bothered by a crowd, yet remains impassive.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is calm, dull and slow to show feeling, which is unemotional.

clue.text: Hanging about in river marsh

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined words are read from the end back

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
a bog is wet marshy ground

explanation.surface: Someone lingers near a riverside swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanging looks like a verb for loitering; it is a noun, a wall hanging. Gobelin tapestries come from the Paris workshop of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gobelin is a tapestry from the famous Paris manufactory, the kind of textile hung on walls.

clue.text: Beastly way for Caesar to address his killer?

definitions.text: way for Caesar to address his killer
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Shakespeare's Caesar says Et tu, ...? to Brutus, using the Latin form of address

explanation.walkthrough: Latin changes a name's ending when someone is spoken to, so Brutus is addressed in Caesar's famous dying words with a different ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning savage or animal, and the form of Brutus used when he is spoken to.

clue.text: Much of life seen in burlesque way up in the mountains

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so the shortened word sits within the comic sketch

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical burlesque

indicators.note: much of a thing is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of existence feels like a farce, spent climbing among high peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable or tow that carries skiers up a slope is a means of ascent among peaks.

clue.text: About a hundred fish at the foot of the column

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the flatfish's letters go round the numeral

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish
C is a hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Around a hundred fish are gathered at the base of a pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is foot of the column alone; at the joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A socle is a plain plinth or block supporting a pillar or statue, its base.

clue.text: Play? Always unpredictable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the comedy by George Bernard Shaw first staged in 1899
second meaning: the saying that the outcome cannot be foreseen

explanation.walkthrough: Play looks like a verb inviting a gamble; it is the title of a Shaw comedy, and the phrase is also an everyday saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw wrote a comedy with this title, and the phrase means nobody can be sure what will happen.

clue.text: Number of legs

parts.note: surface reading: how many legs an animal or a table has
setter's reading: in bingo the caller says legs before announcing one particular number, its two upright digits looking like a pair of legs

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a count of limbs; it is the number whose bingo call begins with legs. Bingo is a numbers game whose callers give each number a rhyme or nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: In bingo the call legs gives this two-digit number, since its upright figures look like a pair of legs.

clue.text: Country's in debt, it's said — not for the first time

definitions.text: said — not for the first time

indicators.note: in puts the nation inside the word for owing money

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt, from red ink in accounts
a state is a country; the 's joins it to the next word

explanation.surface: A nation is reported to be owing money, and not for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate something is to say it again, so it was said once before.
